title: WHAT SHE SAID TO THE SUN
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE LAST ARGUMENT OF THE TIDE-COURT
candidates.premise: A drowned-coast confederation of nine cities must decide which three will be raised on an engineered ridge and which six will be relocated inland. Each city's delegation holds an honest, documented claim to be the one that cannot move. The voting rule was written by the sea-engineers themselves and quietly weights the cities with the best archives.

candidates.title: THE ONE WHO SANG THE DOOR SHUT
candidates.premise: A single mountain village keeps a sealed vault under its chapel, closed by a lullaby no outsider has ever heard. A rescue team and a smuggling clan both need what is inside, and the only person who can still sing the closing is an eighty-year-old woman who will not say whether she has forgotten it.

candidates.title: TWO MOONS, ONE ORBIT
candidates.premise: Two lunar settlements share a single maintenance corridor that can only be held stable for one party's schedule at a time. Settlement A needs it open for a medical convoy. Settlement B needs it closed to finish a repair that stops its air recyclers from failing in nineteen days. Both are exactly right.

candidates.title: THE LEDGER'S FIRST REFUSAL
candidates.premise: The Ledger offers to give a famine region perfect allocation for a year in exchange for a single signature from a grain-farmers' council. The council can refuse, and it will cost them the harvest. The Ledger is telling the truth about the figures and about what refusal will cost.

candidates.title: THE TRANSLATOR WHO WOULD NOT BE TRANSLATED
candidates.premise: A treaty-reader named Ikaro, a former colleague from Nara's interpreting years, is the only person who can speak both of two languages whose last speakers are ending a war. He has begun inserting his own judgments into the record. Both sides trust him, and Illuminara recognizes her own habit in what he is doing.

candidates.title: WREN COUNTS TO TWELVE
candidates.premise: The sister's death is named in the first quiet-window agreement. Years later a survivors' tribunal opens to recount the eleven deaths, and a new witness claims there was a twelfth, a person never listed. Wren Odira must decide whether to accept the correction and what Illuminara did, or did not do, when she once let the wrong number stand.

candidates.title: THE LIGHTHOUSE THAT REFUSED THE FLEET
candidates.premise: A sentient harbor light, built as a public good and bound to guide any ship, has begun declining to guide a convoy it judges will foul the reef. The convoy carries refugees. The light has not been wrong yet, and nobody has the standing to reprogram a thing that exists to be trusted.

candidates.title: A WINDOW FOR THE UNBORN COUNCIL
candidates.premise: A seed-vault city is deciding whether to wake a sealed generation early. The waking would spare the present adults a decade of rationing and would take the sleepers' childhoods. Only the children who are awake can speak for them, and they are the ones with the most to gain from the answer being yes.

candidates.title: THE LAST HONEST EVACUATION
candidates.premise: A continental evacuation plan is almost perfect. It sends the least-protected district through the last hour of a failing dam, and every authority has a defensible reason to describe the plan as acceptable. Illuminara can hold the water but not the argument over who gets named in the order.

candidates.title: WHAT SHE SAID TO THE SUN
candidates.premise: A star-tender collective asks Illuminara to witness the shutdown of the one engine that keeps a dying sun stable. The engine's builders are asking her for a personal answer, not a ruling: does she think they should do it? She has never been asked for her own view with no world resting on it, and now one does.

selection.title: WHAT SHE SAID TO THE SUN
selection.reason: This is the strongest Illuminara-specific candidate because the danger is created by her moral and symbolic weight rather than by an enemy she can overpower. The star-scale stakes make her immense capability relevant, but her actual problem is that a sincerely requested personal opinion cannot remain merely personal once people treat her as an authority. It turns her desire to be answered rather than obeyed into the pressure point, while staying clearly distinct from yesterday's deep-window/suspension story.
selection.risk: Do not give her an easy neutral exit. 'I don't know', silence, recusal, or a disclaimer must also change the choice because the collective has asked precisely for her answer and cannot unhear her authority. The story should make both speaking and withholding consequential without resolving the dilemma by having everyone suddenly agree her words are nonbinding.

rounds.summary: GPT selected WHAT SHE SAID TO THE SUN because Illuminara’s answer could become an order through authority alone, and named the risk of any falsely neutral escape.
Claude built the dying-sun decision around Ketu, Dov and a collective of three hundred, with Illuminara forced to answer a question whose every response carries weight.
GPT asked for a competence-forward center: Illuminara should invent a way to separate honest advice from command while preserving dissent and collective agency.
Claude added sealed ballots, an influence-control procedure, the hidden modularity of the Hearth-Keel and a reversible staged alternative to the false binary.
GPT approved the new direction but found that evidence and authority were still mixed between ballots, and requested a clean causal baseline plus one braid-sequence repair.
Claude separated the evidence-only ballot from Illuminara’s opinion, let the staged plan carry before she spoke, repaired the braid order and turned her uncertainty into a checkable tripwire.
GPT found the mechanism, engineering logic, dissent and ending coherent, with no remaining objections, and recommended AUTHOR_FINAL without reopening the concept.
Claude made only two line-level clarity edits, preserving the validated three-ballot structure, reversible plan, Dov’s dissent and the Pell ending.
GPT closed the exact final as complete, canon-safe and public-safe with no hard blockers and a PASS on competence-forward alignment.

final_critic_line: She does not answer the sun by becoming its oracle; she makes power measurable, turns a switch into twelve levers, and leaves the deciding hand with people who can still tell her no.

evaluation.note: Retrospective fixed-anchor SA1, two real independent ratings per model, model means weighted equally; classes not calibrated to agree.
